ut_black_rocks.blurb: Black Rocks is a small area near Saint George in southwest Utah, climbing short basalt walls. Sport routes make up most of it, with boulder problems, some trad and a few top-ropes alongside. Roped grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, with most at 5.9 and 5.10, and the boulders run from V0 to about V6. Sunny Side faces southeast and holds the most climbs, mostly 5.8 to 5.10, and it turns into a warm spot on cold, sunny winter days. Shady Side faces northwest, is cooler and has routes from 5.8 up to 5.13, mostly around 5.10. Black Rocks Boulders are scattered in the wash between the two sides. Winter is the best season here.

ut_blanding.blurb: Blanding is in San Juan County in southeast Utah, a bit over an hour's drive south of Moab. Climbing here is mostly trad and bouldering, with a few top-rope spots and a little aid, and bolted routes are rare in the vicinity. Boulder problems run from V0 to V4, and the roped climbs are mostly 5.8 to 5.10. Blanding Boulders holds the most climbs: soft sandstone with about fifty established problems, most of them V0 to V3, and room for more. Arch Canyon, Not-Notch Canyon and Prospector Canyon hold the trad and aid lines, and Texas Canyon adds a few more.

wa_morpheus.blurb: Morpheus is a bouldering zone in the Miller River valley near Skykomish, in Washington's central-west Cascades, strung along the old mine road beside the West Fork Miller River. The rock is granodiorite, and every climb here is a boulder problem, with a wide spread from easy to very hard and plenty of moderates. The setting mixes a sun-drenched talus field, a forest thick with devil's club and riverside boulders whose climbability depends on the water level. Most areas have a short approach off the trail. 420 Zone holds the most climbs, followed by Approach Boulders, Lower Devils Club Forest and Washout Boulders. The wider Miller River valley is a junglelike old mining valley.

wi_cox_hollow_2.blurb: Cox Hollow is a bouldering area inside Governor Dodge State Park in southern Wisconsin, with scattered boulders around Cox Hollow Lake, mostly on slopes with a southern aspect. Bouldering makes up nearly all of it, with problems from V0 into the V8 range, most of them V0 to V4. Box Canyon Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Danny's Imaginary Boulders and Boat Landing Boulders. Deutschlander Wall adds a few trad and top-rope lines. The rock in the park is sandstone.

ab_grotto_canyon.blurb: Grotto Canyon lies in the Bow Valley just east of Grotto Mountain, reached from Highway 1A west of Exshaw. It is a sport climbing canyon: nearly all the climbs are bolted, with a few mixed, trad and ice lines. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.13, with most between 5.9 and 5.11. The crags are in shade, and many of the climbs are polished. Hemingway Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Paintings Wall and Water Wall, with The Narrows, Back Door and The Right Wing among the smaller crags.

ab_lake_louise.blurb: Lake Louise is in Banff National Park, Alberta, and most of its climbing is at The Back of The Lake, a set of quartzite buttresses at the far end of the lake that holds nearly all of the climbs. The routes are generally vertical to gently overhanging, a mix of sport and trad, with more sport than trad. Grades run from easy fifth class up to 5.13, with most between 5.10 and 5.12. Lake Louise Ice is a small sub-area of waterfall ice and mixed climbs, and the area also reaches up into alpine routes, so conditions can change quickly.
